# Poissonian logarithmic-time propagators for power-biased quantum resetting

## Finding

**Theorem (logarithmic-time Poisson limit with sharp error and coherence threshold).** Consider the density-matrix channel \(\Phi_t\) generated by the power-biased historical-reset equation defined below, for any finite-dimensional Hermitian Hamiltonian \(H\), resetting rate \(r>0\), and bias parameter \(\beta>0\). Put \(b=1+\beta\). There is a time \(T<\infty\) such that \(\Phi_t\) is invertible as a linear map on all matrices whenever \(t\ge T\). For each \(u\ge0\), define its normalized logarithmic-time propagator by
\[
\Psi_{t,u}=\Phi_{te^u}\circ\Phi_t^{-1}.
\]
For each fixed \(U<\infty\), as \(t\to\infty\),
\[
\sup_{0\le u\le U}\left\|\Psi_{t,u}-\exp\big(bu(\mathcal E_r-\mathrm{Id})\big)\right\|_\diamond=O(t^{-1}),
\qquad
\mathcal E_r(X)=\int_0^\infty r e^{-rs} e^{-iHs}X e^{iHs}\,ds.
\]
The limiting family is a completely positive, trace-preserving (CPTP) semigroup. It is the random-unitary channel obtained by evolving under \(H\) for a compound-Poisson random time, with Poisson rate \(b\) per unit logarithmic time and independent exponential holding times of rate \(r\).

For a nondegenerate qubit with energy separation \(\omega\ne0\) and each \(u>0\), the order \(t^{-1}\) is sharp. Write
\[
\lambda=r+i\omega,\qquad a=\frac{bi\omega}{\lambda},\qquad c=\frac{a(a+1-b)}{\lambda}.
\]
Then \(c\ne0\), and
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}t\left\|\Psi_{t,u}-\exp\big(bu(\mathcal E_r-\mathrm{Id})\big)\right\|_\diamond
=\left|e^{-au}c\right|(1-e^{-u})>0.
\]

There is also a sharp integrated-coherence threshold. For an initial density matrix \(\rho_0\), let \(\Pi_H\) denote pinching onto the eigenspaces of \(H\). If the initial state has nonzero matrix elements connecting distinct energies, let \(\Delta_{\rho_0}\) be the smallest positive absolute energy difference among those elements. Then
\[
\int_1^\infty \left\|\Phi_t(\rho_0)-\Pi_H(\rho_0)\right\|_2\,dt<\infty
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\beta>\frac{r^2}{\Delta_{\rho_0}^2}.
\]
At equality the integral diverges logarithmically; below equality it diverges by a power. If no distinct-energy coherence is present, the integrand vanishes identically.

## Assumptions and scope

Fix an integer \(d\ge1\) and a Hermitian matrix \(H\in\mathbb C^{d\times d}\). In units with \(\hbar=1\), the ensemble mean of a unitary system subject to historical-state resetting is defined by the linear initial-value equation
\[
\frac{d\rho_t}{dt}=-i[H,\rho_t]-r\rho_t+
 r\frac{b}{t^b}\int_0^t s^{b-1}\rho_s\,ds,
\qquad \rho_{t=0}=\rho_0,
\qquad b=1+\beta>1.
\]
The normalized sampling density is \(K(s,t)=bs^{b-1}/t^b\) for \(0<s<t\), i.e. resetting favors more recent times. Write \(\rho_t=\Phi_t(\rho_0)\). On every reset history, there is a nonnegative operational clock \(S_t\) which advances at speed one between resets and jumps to its value at a sampled earlier time when a reset occurs. The trajectory state remains \(e^{-iH S_t}\rho_0e^{iH S_t}\); the clock law is independent of the input state. Thus \(\Phi_t\) is a mixture of unitary conjugations and is CPTP. This also agrees with positivity obtained by successive positive approximations to the Volterra equation. We treat finite-dimensional systems and all initial density matrices. The diamond norm is the completely bounded trace norm; \(\|X\|_2=(\operatorname{Tr}X^\dagger X)^{1/2}\).

The quantity \(\Psi_{t,u}\) is a *linear normalized propagator*. For a finite \(t\), the inverse \(\Phi_t^{-1}\) need not be a physical quantum operation and \(\Psi_{t,u}\) need not be CPTP. The theorem asserts convergence to a CPTP semigroup, not exact finite-time CP-divisibility.

## Proof

**1. Exact scalar modes and nonzero leading amplitude.** Choose an eigenbasis \(H|j\rangle=E_j|j\rangle\), and set \(\omega=E_j-E_k\). The channel acts diagonally on matrix units:
\[
\Phi_t(|j\rangle\langle k|)=f_{b,r}(\omega,t)|j\rangle\langle k|.
\]
The scalar Volterra equation is
\[
 f'(t)=-(r+i\omega)f(t)+\frac{rb}{t^b}\int_0^t s^{b-1}f(s)\,ds,\qquad f(0)=1.
\]
The normalized average tends to \(f(0)\) at the origin, so \(f'(0)=-i\omega\). Differentiate after multiplication by \(t^b\), obtaining
\[
 t f''(t)+\big(b+(r+i\omega)t\big)f'(t)+bi\omega f(t)=0.
\]
Its regular solution, also uniquely solving the Volterra equation, is
\[
 f_{b,r}(\omega,t)={}_1F_1\!\left(\frac{bi\omega}{r+i\omega};b;-(r+i\omega)t\right).
\]
For \(\omega=0\), this equals one. For \(\omega\ne0\), write \(\lambda=r+i\omega\) and \(a=bi\omega/\lambda\). The confluent-hypergeometric large-argument expansion, valid on the present ray because \(\operatorname{Re}\lambda>0\), gives
\[
 f_{b,r}(\omega,t)=C_{b,r,\omega}\,t^{-a}\left(1+\frac{c}{t}+O(t^{-2})\right),
\quad C_{b,r,\omega}=\frac{\Gamma(b)}{\Gamma(b-a)}\lambda^{-a},\quad c=\frac{a(a+1-b)}{\lambda}.
\]
Here the complex power uses the principal logarithm. The exponentially decaying contribution is absorbed in the error. The coefficient \(c\) follows by inserting \(t^{-a}(1+c/t)\) into the differential equation and matching the next power. Moreover \(\operatorname{Re}(b-a)=br^2/(r^2+\omega^2)>0\). Gamma has no zero, hence \(C_{b,r,\omega}\ne0\). For every nonzero \(\omega\), also \(c\ne0\): \(a\ne0\) and \(a+1-b=0\) would require \(r+i\omega=br\), impossible for nonzero real \(\omega\). Since the spectrum has finitely many Bohr frequencies, every scalar channel eigenvalue is nonzero at all sufficiently large times, proving invertibility.

**2. A random-unitary limiting semigroup.** On the same matrix unit, \(\mathcal E_r\) acts by multiplication by \(r/(r+i\omega)\). Therefore \(\exp(bu(\mathcal E_r-\mathrm{Id}))\) acts by \(e^{-au}\). The preceding scalar expansion gives, uniformly for \(u\) in any bounded nonnegative interval,
\[
\frac{f_{b,r}(\omega,te^u)}{f_{b,r}(\omega,t)}
=e^{-au}\left[1+\frac{c(e^{-u}-1)}{t}+O(t^{-2})\right].
\]
For \(\omega=0\), the ratio and target eigenvalue equal one. Finitely many matrix units and equivalence of superoperator norms imply the claimed uniform \(O(t^{-1})\) diamond-norm bound. The identification as a CPTP semigroup is explicit:
\[
\exp\big(bu(\mathcal E_r-\mathrm{Id})\big)
=e^{-bu}\sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{(bu)^n}{n!}\mathcal E_r^n.
\]
Each \(\mathcal E_r^n\) is a convex average of unitary conjugations with a sum of \(n\) independent exponential holding times. The Poisson weights sum to one. Thus every limiting map is CPTP and the semigroup law follows from the exponential.

**3. Sharp qubit diamond error.** For \(d=2\), the difference between normalized propagator and limiting channel annihilates the diagonal and multiplies the upper off-diagonal entry by a complex scalar \(\delta_t\), with the conjugate factor on the lower entry. This Hermiticity-preserving difference has diamond norm exactly \(|\delta_t|\): a superposition pure state attains that trace norm, and the map is \(|\delta_t|/2\) times a difference of two diagonal-unitary conjugations, giving the matching upper bound even with an ancilla. The scalar expansion above yields
\[
\delta_t=e^{-au}\frac{c(e^{-u}-1)}{t}+O(t^{-2}).
\]
The resulting nonzero coefficient is the stated sharp limit.

**4. Exact integrability boundary.** Let \(\Delta_{\rho_0}>0\) be the smallest active nonzero Bohr frequency magnitude. Because
\[
\operatorname{Re}a=\frac{b\omega^2}{r^2+\omega^2}
\]
is strictly increasing with \(|\omega|>0\), the slowest initial inter-energy coherences have decay exponent \(\sigma_*=b\Delta_{\rho_0}^2/(r^2+\Delta_{\rho_0}^2)\). Orthogonality of matrix units in Hilbert-Schmidt norm and the nonvanishing constants from Step 1 yield the strictly positive finite limit
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}t^{\sigma_*}\|\Phi_t(\rho_0)-\Pi_H(\rho_0)\|_2
=\left(\sum_{|E_j-E_k|=\Delta_{\rho_0}}|\rho_{0,jk}|^2|C_{b,r,E_j-E_k}|^2\right)^{1/2}>0.
\]
The improper time integral converges exactly when \(\sigma_*>1\), equivalent to \(\beta>r^2/\Delta_{\rho_0}^2\). Equality gives a logarithmic divergence. This concludes the proof.

## Verification

Execute `python verify.py` after installing the packages in `requirements.txt`. The verifier tests the exact scalar solution against a separately time-stepped history-integral equation; checks the differentiated equation; checks Hermitian and positive-semidefinite finite-time Schur matrices on multilevel examples; compares normalized finite-time ratios to their independently derived compound-Poisson characteristic functions; and checks both the sharp first-order qubit coefficient and the Hilbert-Schmidt asymptotic exponent. The executed result was:

`VERIFY_OK 215 ODE/Volterra, CPTP Schur, Poisson log-time, sharp Hilbert-Schmidt exponent`

Numerical testing is finite and does not prove the universal theorem. Steps 1–4 provide its mathematical proof.

## Relationship to prior work

De Mauro, Kulkarni and Majumdar [1] derived the exact uniform-memory (\(b=1\)) quantum channel multipliers and their algebraic, logarithmically oscillating coherences; they explicitly leave nonuniform quantum memory kernels open. Boyer and collaborators [2,3] established classical preferential-relocation kernels, including precisely the power-kernel confluent-hypergeometric scalar equation for positive *diffusion* eigenvalues. **The scalar special-function manipulation alone is not claimed as original**; it transfers directly by the imaginary-frequency substitution. The present structural claim concerns the resulting quantum normalized propagators: their finite-dimensional uniform diamond-norm approximation by a completely positive compound-Poisson semigroup, a sharp nonzero qubit error coefficient, and a state-dependent summable-coherence threshold. The sources [1–3] do not state these quantum-channel conclusions. Siudzińska and Chruściński [4] study a different, translation-invariant convolution-kernel master equation for generalized Pauli channels, not this two-time historical-state sampling protocol. Related non-Markovian resetting [5] treats waiting-time renewal with a fixed reset state, not a preferentially selected past quantum state.

## Limitations

Finite matrix dimension is essential to the uniform inversion and diamond-norm statement; this proof does not establish an infinite-dimensional analogue. The limiting semigroup acts in logarithmic time and does not assert actual finite-time Markovianity or physical implementability of \(\Phi_t^{-1}\). The sharp diamond coefficient is established explicitly for qubits, not as an exact coefficient for all higher dimensions. The integrated-coherence threshold is for the Hilbert-Schmidt distance to energy pinching, not for arbitrary observables, trajectories, or an environmental entropy measure. This is a mathematical analysis of the specified history-reset model; no experimental realizability or implementation robustness is claimed. An earlier implicit derivation from classical kernel formulas and general quantum-channel methods remains a possible priority risk.
